title: Natural Gas Power Plant Ordinance Extraction Schema
description: Extract enacted siting requirements for natural gas-fired power plants that generate electricity for offsite sale or grid delivery.

feature.description: The supported ordinance feature, using exactly one of these IDs.
enum: minimum lot width to depth ratio

value.description: One value selected under value_selection: a number for numerical requirements, a string for a lot ratio, or a nonempty array of names/codes for a district-list feature. Omit unsupported features rather than returning null-valued or empty rows.

units.description: Use 'feet', 'miles', 'acres', 'square feet', 'percent', 'dBA', 'dBC', or 'MW' as specified for the feature. Use null for district lists, ratios and effective year.

section.description: The section number/title or table establishing the selected requirement. Retain subsection and table-note identifiers. Use null only when none is supplied.

summary.description: Use at most three concise sentences (aim for 60 words before the list) citing the governing use, its approval status and use provision, and the applicable standard. Prefer short exact quotes; include only conditions that affect this feature. For numerical requirements and lot ratios, end with 'District values: ' and entries separated by '; '. Entry format: '<district codes> = <value> <units> (<condition>)'. Omit units for ratios and omit parentheses when unnecessary. Put the selected entry first and mark it '[selected]'; retain tied districts. Group districts only when their value, units and conditions agree. Include every eligible district, using 'not stated' for a missing applicable value or 'no requirement' only when explicitly stated. Never include prohibited or unverified districts. Use 'facility-wide' only for an explicit plant-specific requirement with no established district list. Keep other district values and same-feature alternatives, with short qualifiers for yard type, measurement basis, receptor, time period or 'if <circumstance>'. Preserve conditions and any different supporting section/source; do not invent a numeric waiver or reduction. Use exact district codes, or names if no codes exist, and numbers without thousands separators. Do not repeat the list in the prose. District-list and effective-year rows use concise prose only, without a District values list.

source.description: The zero-based integer from the '# SOURCE INDEX #' marker of the document supplying the selected requirement, not a URL or section number. Identify any different supporting source and provision in the summary. Use null only when no source index is supplied.

facility_scope.description: Natural gas-fired electric generating plants producing electricity for offsite sale or grid delivery, including simple-cycle, combined-cycle, peaking and cogeneration plants where power export is a primary purpose. Exclude requirements solely for other generating technologies or fuels, onsite emergency/standby/backup generators, gas extraction or drilling, pipelines, compressor or metering stations, gas storage, LNG/CNG or propane facilities, fueling stations and building gas equipment. General electric-generation or utility provisions qualify only through district_eligibility.

district_eligibility.description: Use the combined supplied documents. First identify the governing use: prefer a natural-gas generating use, then an electric generating or power-plant use covering natural gas. Only if no specific generating use is supplied may a listed public-utility or nongovernmental-utility use govern, provided it is not restricted to non-generating infrastructure. Do not combine broader utility permissions with a specific generating-use row to expand eligibility. Establish permitted, conditional or special-use districts from the operative use list/table with its headings, legend and footnotes. Do not infer permission from industrial zoning, dimensions, an existing plant or a general utility exemption. Missing or illegible table cells do not establish permission; blanks establish prohibition only when the ordinance says so. Do not assume government ownership, accessory status or a size exemption to expand the ordinary plant category. Summarize any explicit exemption or state-authority limitation without assuming it applies to every plant. An explicit plant-specific requirement or prohibition may be extracted without a district list. Otherwise, without a governing use and eligible districts, return {"outputs": []}; missing evidence is not proof of prohibition.

setback_features.description: Distances for the principal generating facility, with measurement endpoints retained in the summary

residential dwellings.description: Setback from occupied dwellings, habitable structures or places of public assembly. VALUE: number. UNITS: 'feet' or 'miles'. IGNORE: residential zoning boundaries, property lines and setbacks solely for accessory structures.

property line.description: Setback from lot or parcel boundaries, including side and rear yards. VALUE: number. UNITS: 'feet'. Distinguish side and rear requirements in the summary. IGNORE: front yards and road setbacks unless the same provision expressly covers all property lines.

residential district.description: Setback from a residentially zoned district boundary. VALUE: number. UNITS: 'feet' or 'miles'. Preserve any population-center or other geographic qualifier. IGNORE: distances to individual dwellings.

front yard.description: Front-yard setback for the facility. VALUE: number. UNITS: 'feet'. IGNORE: side and rear yards. Preserve whether measurement starts at a lot line, right-of-way or road centerline.

street.description: Setback from a street, road, right-of-way or street easement centerline. VALUE: number. UNITS: 'feet'. A front-yard requirement expressly measured from a street right-of-way or centerline belongs here as well as under front yard. IGNORE: easement widths, frontage lengths and front-yard values without an explicit road measurement.

numerical_restrictions.description: Applicable plant dimensional and performance requirements

generation capacity.description: An explicit generating-capacity applicability threshold or maximum limit. VALUE: number. UNITS: 'MW'. Identify which meaning applies in the summary; do not compare a threshold and a cap as interchangeable limits. IGNORE: descriptive capacity of an existing or proposed project without an operative requirement.

maximum building height.description: Maximum building or structure height above ground or final grade. VALUE: number. UNITS: 'feet'. Use the dimensional row covering the governing use, not a broader all-uses row when a utility-specific row applies. IGNORE: heights solely for other uses; keep stack, tower and other height exceptions in the summary.

minimum lot size.description: Minimum parcel area for the governing use. VALUE: number. UNITS: 'acres' or 'square feet' as stated. IGNORE: linear dimensions and zero entries meaning no fixed minimum. Water/sewer-dependent minimums belong in the summary as circumstance-specific alternatives.

minimum lot width.description: Minimum lot width at the ordinance's specified measurement line. VALUE: number. UNITS: 'feet'. IGNORE: street frontage, road widths and lot depth.

minimum lot frontage.description: Minimum parcel frontage along a street or road. VALUE: number. UNITS: 'feet'. IGNORE: lot width measured at a building line and road/easement widths.

minimum lot width to depth ratio.description: Required lot width-to-depth relationship. VALUE: string such as '1:2'. UNITS: null. Preserve the direction of the constraint (for example maximum depth relative to width) in the summary. IGNORE: unrelated building or floor-area ratios.

maximum lot coverage.description: Maximum share of a lot covered by buildings or impervious surface. VALUE: number. UNITS: 'percent'. Identify the regulated surface in the summary. IGNORE: minimum coverage, floor-area ratios and landscaping/open-space percentages; do not derive coverage by subtraction.

noise (dBA).description: A-weighted noise limit. VALUE: number. UNITS: 'dBA'. Retain source district, receptor location, measurement/averaging method and any day/night alternatives in the summary. IGNORE: unweighted decibels and C-weighted limits.

noise (dBC).description: C-weighted noise limit. VALUE: number. UNITS: 'dBC'. Retain source district, receptor location, measurement/averaging method and any day/night alternatives in the summary. IGNORE: unweighted decibels and A-weighted limits.

permitted_use_districts.description: Mutually consistent classifications for the same governing use and ordinary facility conditions; use exact ordinance district names/codes

primary use districts.description: Districts permitting the governing use by right or as a principal permitted use. VALUE: nonempty array of district names/codes. UNITS: null. Site plan review, site development plan approval and building permits alone are standard permitting, not special approval. IGNORE: districts requiring a conditional-use permit, special-use permit or special exception; omit the feature if none qualify.

special use districts.description: Districts requiring conditional-use approval, a special-use permit or a special exception for the governing use. VALUE: nonempty array of district names/codes. UNITS: null. Name the required approval in the summary. IGNORE: routine site plan review or building permits alone; omit the feature if none qualify.

prohibited use districts.description: Districts unconditionally prohibiting the ordinary governing use, explicitly or through an operative prohibition-by-omission rule. VALUE: nonempty array of district names/codes. UNITS: null. Cite the prohibition or table legend in the summary. IGNORE: temporary expired bans, districts allowing that use in any approval category, and missing evidence without a prohibition rule; omit the feature if none qualify.

effective_year.description: ordinance effective year: the explicitly stated effective year of an applicable enacted ordinance. VALUE: four-digit number. UNITS: null. A history-note date qualifies when the code explicitly defines those dates as effective dates. IGNORE: proposed dates, website update dates and historical dates without that evidence. Omit if not stated; never emit an effective-year-only result.

$instructions.scope: Extract only the enumerated siting features for plants in facility_scope. Definitions may establish the governing use but are not requirements by themselves. Apply district_eligibility before emitting rows.
applicability: Match each eligible district to the dimensional/performance provisions for the principal generating use, including applicable general commercial/industrial standards. Do not use residential, agricultural, mixed-use housing, accessory-building, sign, parking or loading-area rows as plant requirements.

Apply table headings, footnotes and cross-references before choosing values. If conditional or special-exception dimensions are assigned to another section, use that section, not the displaced table. Retain independently applicable general standards. A missing redirected provision means 'not stated', not permission to borrow a table value.
Use only enacted provisions in effect. Where supplied amendments explicitly replace a provision, use the amended requirement; do not treat a superseded value as another district option.
value_selection: Return one object per supported feature, with no district field or duplicate feature rows. District-list features contain all qualifying districts, not a selected district. Omit unsupported features, null placeholders and rows whose only finding is 'none', 'N/A' or 'no requirement'. If only circumstance-specific values are supplied and no base requirement is stated, omit the feature rather than selecting an exception.

For numerical requirements, select the most restrictive generally applicable stated value among eligible districts: largest setbacks and minimum lot dimensions; smallest maximum height, coverage and noise limits. Include alternative yard types, measurement bases, receptors and time periods in the comparison, preserving their conditions in the summary. Missing values in other eligible districts do not block extraction and are listed as 'not stated'; never infer their values. A provision allowing utilities or public uses in any or all zones by permit (such as a public use permit) is not a district-level permission. Report it in the district-list row as a single entry 'All zones (<permit name>)' instead of listing every district, and exclude those districts from numerical value selection. Select numerical values only from districts whose own use list or use table permits the governing use.

Additional geographic overlays, subdivision-only standards, private-road access, wells/septic, ownership-specific exemptions, waivers, variances, discretionary buffers and reductions are circumstance-specific, not the base value. Keep their explicit values and conditions only in the summary of an otherwise supported feature. Do not assume that every plant site is in an additional overlay or requires subdivision. A governing district's dimensional-table condition, such as not adjoining residential uses, must accompany its values; it does not justify discarding the whole table.

Compare compatible quantities in common units but retain each reported value in its source units using the units vocabulary. Do not compare raw numbers across acres/square feet or miles/feet. For ratios and capacity, respect the direction and meaning of the stated requirement, and preserve alternatives rather than inventing an ordering between unlike constraints. For formula-based requirements, retain any explicit fixed floor or cap and describe the formula without assuming missing inputs.
$instructions.summary: Follow the summary field description. Keep district alternatives and relevant exceptions concise, with their measurement conditions and supporting provisions. Do not reproduce unrelated permit procedures, monitoring requirements or rejected-use explanations.
$instructions.examples: The following examples illustrate format only. Their districts, values and sections are synthetic; never use them as evidence or copy them into another jurisdiction.

$examples.summary: Sec. 2 permits gas-fired power plants in I-2 and conditionally in I-1 and A-1; Sec. 4 sets industrial front yards. A-1's table covers residential development only. District values: I-2 = 75 feet [selected]; I-1 = 50 feet; I-1 = 100 feet (if accessing a private road, Sec. 6); A-1 = not stated.

Sec. 2 permits the governing utility use in I-1 and I-2 with site plan review, and by special exception in A-1. Sec. 4 supplies the utility lot minimums; its note redirects A-1 to design provisions not supplied. District values: I-2 = 2 acres [selected]; I-1 = 20000 square feet; A-1 = not stated.

Sec. 2 permits gas-fired plants in I-2 and conditionally in I-1. Sec. 8 limits hourly plant noise at the receiving property boundary. District values: I-1, I-2 = 50 dBA (residential receptor at night) [selected]; I-1, I-2 = 55 dBA (residential receptor by day); I-1, I-2 = 60 dBA (nonresidential receptor).

Sec. 9 requires gas-fired generating plants to maintain a setback from occupied dwellings; no district list is supplied. District values: facility-wide = 1200 feet (plant outer wall to dwelling) [selected].
